newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end mixed at start of Hindu new year.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end mixed at start of Hindu new year.

text.p: ** Indian shares end mixed on Sunday in special "moorat" trading session to mark start of Hindu New Year
** Traders say funds pick nominal amounts to mark auspicious day but volumes are operator-driven
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index ends at 3080.26 against 3066.66 but the 50-share index of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) finishes 5.0 points down at 880 points
** Calcutta and Delhi bourses end lower
** Former Finance Minister Manmohan Singh says worried by signs of economic slowdown
** India relaxes norms for foreign investment in debt
Indian shares finished mixed on Sunday in a special festive session to mark the start of the Hindu new year, traders said.
"We hope to start the new year on a better note," said Zubin Tampal, dealer at Bombay broker Motilal Oswal. "The year that went by was a dismal one."
Traders say funds picked nominal amounts in the "moorat" session to mark the auspicious day but volumes were largely operator driven.
Former Finance Minister Manmohan Singh said on Saturday he was worried by signs of a slowdown in the economy.
Singh, the architect of India's economic reforms programme which began in 1991, told an independent television channel he was worried by signs of a slowdown in the domestic economy.
Singh said the diverse nature of the ruling centre-left coalition government made investors nervous.
He said investor confidence had not anything to do with the specific policies of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition government but with its composition.
"The fact that you have thirteen political parties. The fact that their ministers often don't speak in the same voice. I think all this does cause nervousness," he said.

India on Saturday relaxed norms for foreign investment in debt. Market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India said foreign institutional investors (FIIs) will be allowed to invest their entire portfolio in Indian debt instruments against the existing cap of 30 percent.
In Calcutta, the index ended 1.45 points lower at 411.87.
The Delhi stocks index finished 4.13 points down at 690.35.
"Activity was confined to very few counters as investors booked profits even at low levels in the absence of any institutional buying," said Sumit Gandhi of brokers Rare Financial services in Delhi.
